function: End-to-end bit transmission: learned modulation and demodulation DNNs plus SIM wave-domain precoding and combining, trained to minimize BER from transmitted to received bits (p. 1, p. 7, p. 8).
system: Downlink OFDM: 16-antenna BS with 3-layer TX-SIM, 3 UEs with 9 antennas and 3-layer RX-SIM, 100 elements per layer; stacked RIS; 28 GHz, 100 MHz (p. 3, p. 11).
method: EMNN: BS-DNN, UE-DNN and trainable SIM phase layers, autoencoder-style end-to-end training with BCE loss and mini-batch SGD; transfer learning: statistical-CSI pretraining, instantaneous-CSI fine-tuning (p. 8-9).
data_channel: Own geometric multipath channel (100 scatterers, LoS plus NLoS) with path loss of [51]; random bit vectors; no 3GPP model or measured data (p. 5, p. 11).
test_conditions: Pretrained on statistical channel, fine-tuned on each random instantaneous channel set; BER averaged over sets, with curves for different transmit power, SIM size, layers, antennas, subcarriers (p. 9-12).
baselines: E2E-optimized massive MIMO OFDM with 256 TX antennas (BER); complexity versus hybrid-precoding E2E; own ablations and training variants; no non-learned baseline (p. 10-12).
metrics: BER versus transmit power; training loss (BCE) versus epochs; FLOPs, parameter and forward complexity orders; fine-tuning time in ms (p. 10-12).
complexity: Parameters O(ML+NKJ+D^2HJ); forward O(Nc(M^2L+N^2KJ)+D^2HJ); about 2.3e7 FLOPs and 15 ms fine-tuning for L=3, M=100; 92% below fully digital (p. 10).
openness: GitHub repository linked in the first-page footnote: https://github.com/ZhangYida02/Stacked_Intelligent_Metasurfaces_for_End-to-End_OFDM_System (p. 1).
q1_support: p. 5: "geometric multi-path channel model" with S scatterers; p. 11: path loss "modeled by [51]" (Rappaport et al.), scatterers per [50]. Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "a base model is first trained using the statistical CSI", then fine-tuned; p. 10: "multiple sets of instantaneous channels are randomly generated" and fine-tuned per set; p. 11: "the average of the test results under different channel conditions".
q3_support: p. 10: "two state-of-the-art E2E OFDM schemes" (fully digital and hybrid precoding, both E2E-learned) and p. 11: "comparable performance to a massive MIMO OFDM system with 256T49R" (E2E-optimized per Table II); no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "forward propagation computational complexity" given as O(Nc(M^2 L + N^2 KJ) + D^2 HJ), "only takes about 15 ms" of fine-tuning, about 2.3e7 FLOPs per forward pass.
q5_support: p. 1: "Data is available on-line at https://github.com/ZhangYida02" (repository Stacked_Intelligent_Metasurfaces_for_End-to-End_OFDM_System, footnote on the first page).
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Included: learned E2E OFDM transceiver (DNNs plus trainable SIM phases), multi-antenna, BER results. Area 1 follows the main-metric rule (BER); area 3 is the alternative because the learned SIM phases act as precoder and combiner. q1: custom geometric channel, path loss from [51]. q2 is borderline: it rests only on fine-tuning from statistical CSI to new instantaneous channels (p. 9-11); no other scenario, band or dataset is tested, and the power sweep of Fig. 8 does not count. q3: massive MIMO baseline is E2E-optimized (Table II), no ZF or MMSE baseline. q5: the link was not opened, so the repository content is not verified.
